# `Q-2-59` — Indented code blocks are not supported

> Quarto Markdown does not support 4-space indented code blocks. Use a
> fenced code block (```` ``` ````) instead, or remove the leading
> indentation.

## What this means

In CommonMark, a paragraph-level line indented four or more spaces (or
one tab) starts an *indented code block*. Quarto Markdown has no such
block: only fenced code blocks are code. Rather than silently turning
indented text into code, the parser reports this error.

This code was previously reported as `Q-2-35`, which now means only an
invalid list-table structure (see [`Q-2-35`](Q-2-35.qmd)).

## Why this happens

- **Documents ported from Pandoc or CommonMark** that use indentation
  to mark code.
- **Accidental indentation**, such as a pasted block or a paragraph
  continued with four leading spaces after a blank line.
- **Writer output** that indents a continuation, for example the second
  paragraph of a footnote.

## How to fix

Use a fenced code block:

````markdown
```
foo
```
````

If the indentation was accidental, remove it so the line starts at
column zero, or at most three spaces in.
